source: Dallas City Code ch. 51P, Article 1040 (City Attorney's codified article, April 2026)

sections.title: Legislative History
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-1040.101. LEGISLATIVE HISTORY.

PD 1040 was established by Ordinance No. 31693, passed by the Dallas City Council on November 11, 2020. (Ord. 31693)

sections.title: Property Location And Size
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-1040.102. PROPERTY LOCATION AND SIZE.

PD 1040 is established on property located at the northwest corner of Lancaster Road and Crouch Road. The size of PD 1040 is approximately 63.458 acres. (Ord. 31693)

sections.title: Definitions And Interpretations
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-1040.103. DEFINITIONS AND INTERPRETATIONS.

(a) Unless otherwise stated, the definitions and interpretations in Chapter 51A apply to this article.

(b) Unless otherwise stated, all references to articles, divisions, or sections in this article are to articles, divisions, or sections in Chapter 51A.

(c) This district is considered to be a nonresidential zoning district. (Ord. 31693)

sections.title: Exhibits
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-1040.104. EXHIBITS.

The following exhibits are incorporated into this article:

(1) Exhibit 1040A: conceptual plan.

(2) Exhibit 1040B: Tract 1 development plan. (Ord. 31693)

sections.title: Conceptual Plan
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-1040.105. CONCEPTUAL PLAN.

Development and use of the Property must comply with the conceptual plan (Exhibit 1040A). If there is a conflict between the text of this article and the conceptual plan, the text of this article controls. (Ord. 31693)

sections.title: Development Plan
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-1040.106. DEVELOPMENT PLAN.

(a) For uses in Tract 1, development and use of the Property must comply with the Tract 1 development plan (Exhibit 1040B). If there is a conflict between the text of this article and the Tract 1 development plan, the text of this article controls.

(b) Except as provided in this section, for all other tracts, a development plan must be approved by the city plan commission before the issuance of any building permit to authorize work in this district. If there is a conflict between the text of this article and the development plan, the text of this article controls.

(c) For single family uses, a final plat may serve as the development plan in all phases of development.

(d) Building permits for a driveway in Tract 4 may be issued without the approval of a development plan.

(e) Accessory community center (private) is not required to be shown on the development plan.

(f) Accessory structures such as, gazebos, game courts, playgrounds, pools, and trellises are not required to be shown on the development plan. (Ord. 31693)

sections.title: Main Uses Permitted
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-1040.107. MAIN USES PERMITTED.

(a) In general. Except as provided in this section, the only main uses permitted are those main uses permitted in the MU-1 Mixed Use District, subject to the same conditions applicable in the MU-1 Mixed Use District, as set out in Chapter 51A. For example, a use permitted in the MU-1 Mixed Use District only by specific use permit (SUP) is permitted in this district only by SUP; a use subject to development impact review (DIR) in the MU-1 Mixed Use District is subject to DIR in this district; etc.

(b) Tract 1. The following uses are the only main uses permitted: -- Handicapped group dwelling unit. -- Local utilities. -- Multifamily -- Retirement housing. -- Single family.

(c) Tract 2. The following uses are the only main uses permitted:

-- Handicapped group dwelling unit. -- Local utilities. -- Multifamily. -- Single family.

(d) Tracts 3 and 4. Residential uses are prohibited.

(e) Prohibited uses. The following main uses are prohibited in all tracts:

-- Auto service center. -- Car wash. -- Cemetery or mausoleum. -- Commercial amusement (outside). -- Commercial parking lot or garage. -- Labor hall. -- Mini-warehouse. -- Mortuary, funeral home, or commercial wedding chapel. -- Motor vehicle fueling station. -- Recycling buy-back center. -- Swap or buy shop. (Ord. 31693)

sections.title: Accessory Uses
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-1040.108. ACCESSORY USES.

(a) As a general rule, an accessory use is permitted in any district in which the main use is permitted. Some specific accessory uses, however, due to their unique nature, are subject to additional regulations in Section 51A-4.217. For more information regarding accessory uses, consult Section 51A-4.217.

(b) Accessory community center (private) is permitted by right.

(c) Multifamily uses in Tract 1 must include a minimum of 500 square feet of accessory storage, a minimum of one swimming pool, one playground, and one accessory community center (private). (Ord. 31693)

sections.title: Yard, Lot, And Space Regulations
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-1040.109. YARD, LOT, AND SPACE REGULATIONS.

(Note: The yard, lot, and space regulations in this section must be read together with the yard, lot, and space regulations in Division 51A-4.400. If there is a conflict between this section and Division 51A-4.400, this section controls.)

(a) In general. Except as provided in this section, the yard, lot, and space regulations for the MU-1 Mixed Use District apply.

(b) Front yard.

(1) Except as provided in this subsection, minimum front yard is 15 feet.

(2) For multifamily structures along Crouch Road, maximum front yard is 50 feet.

(3) Encroachments such as awnings, balconies, bay windows, ramps, retaining walls, stairs, stoops, and unenclosed porches are allowed in the required front yard and are not required to be shown on the development plan.

(c) Side and rear yard. No side or rear yard is required.

(d) Density.

(1) Tract 1. Maximum number of dwelling units is 300.

(2) Tract 2. Maximum number of dwelling units is 300.

(e) Floor area ratio. Maximum floor area ratio for non-residential uses in Tracts 3 and 4 is 0.4.

(f) Height.

(1) Maximum height.

(A) Except as provided in this section, maximum structure height is 36 feet.

(B) Chimneys may project up to 12 feet above the maximum structure height.

(2) Residential proximity slope.

(A) If any portion of a structure is over 26 feet in height, that portion may not be located above a residential proximity slope originating in an R, R(A), D, D(A), TH, or TH(A) district (see Section 51A-4.412).

(B) The following structures may project up to 12 feet above the residential proximity slope:

(i) Elevator penthouse or bulkhead.

(ii) Mechanical equipment room.

(iii) Cooling tower.

(iv) Tank designed to hold liquids.

(v) Ornamental cupola or dome.

(vi) Skylights.

(vii) Clerestory.

(viii) Visual screens which surround roof mounted mechanical equipment.

(ix) Chimneys and vent stacks.

(x) Amateur communications tower.

(xi) Parapet wall, limited to a height of four feet.

(g) Lot coverage. Maximum lot coverage is 60 percent. Aboveground parking structures are included in lot coverage calculations; surface parking lots and underground parking structures are not.

(h) Stories. Maximum number of stories above grade is three. (Ord. 31693)

sections.title: Off-Street Parking And Loading
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-1040.110. OFF-STREET PARKING AND LOADING.

Except as provided in Section 51P-1040.114, consult the use regulations in Division 51A- 4.200 for the specific off-street parking and loading requirements for each use. (Ord. 31693)

sections.title: Environmental Performance Standards
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-1040.111. ENVIRONMENTAL PERFORMANCE STANDARDS.

See Article VI. (Ord. 31693)

sections.title: Landscaping
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-1040.112. LANDSCAPING.

(a) Landscaping must be provided in accordance with Article X.

(b) Plant materials must be maintained in a healthy, growing condition. (Ord. 31693)

sections.title: Design Standards
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-1040.113. DESIGN STANDARDS.

(a) Fencing.

(1) Fences along Crouch Road and Lancaster Road must be:

(A) a maximum of six feet in height;

(A) constructed of brick, stone, decorative block, wrought iron, tubular steel, wood, or similar materials, or a combination of these materials; and

(B) no more than 50 percent opaque.

(2) For fences along Crouch Road, pedestrian gates or pedestrian access at vehicular ingress and egress points must be provided for every 150 feet of fence length.

(b) Sidewalks.

(1) Minimum unobstructed sidewalk width of six feet is required along Crouch Road and Lancaster Road.

(2) Before the issuance of a certificate of occupancy in Tract 1, a minimum six- foot-wide sidewalk must be constructed within the Crouch Road right-of-way that connects the Property with the Runyon Creek Trail, subject to approval by the director. The director may approve a reduction of the minimum sidewalk width if the existing right-of-way is not sufficient.

(c) Pedestrian lighting. Pedestrian scale lighting must be provided for every 50 feet of sidewalk along Crouch Road. Pedestrian lighting must:

(1) provide a minimum of 1.5 footcandles; and

(2) be mounted at a height no greater than 14 feet.

(d) Structures.

(1) Crouch Road.

(A) Individual entries. For multifamily structures located within 50 feet of the Crouch Road right-of-way, each structure must have street facing doors with a walkway that connects to the Crouch Road sidewalk.

(B) Building placement. A minimum of 60 percent of multifamily structures must located between the minimum and maximum front yard. Driveways, visibility triangles, and floodplain easements are excluded from the frontage calculation.

(2) Tract 2.

(A) Multifamily structures must have a minimum of three dwelling units and dwelling units must be constructed side-by-side, not stacked vertically, with doors opening to an outdoor walkway.

(B) Primary facades and primary entrances of dwelling units that are located along the DART right-of-way must be oriented to face the DART right-of-way.

(e) Open space. In Tract 1, a dog park is required to be located within the open space shown on the development plan. (Ord. 31693)

sections.title: Development Bonus
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-1040.114. DEVELOPMENT BONUS.

(a) If a minimum of five percent of the total number of dwelling units in Tract 1 are provided at Income Band 3 and in compliance with Division 51A-4.1100, and individual garages are provided in accordance with Subsection (b), multifamily uses may provide reduced parking in the amount of a minimum 1.5 off-street parking spaces per dwelling unit.

(b) A minimum of 32 individual garages are required for multifamily uses and may count towards the minimum parking requirement.

(c) Compliance with Section 51A-4.1107 is not required. (Ord. 31693)

sections.title: Signs
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-1040.115. SIGNS.

Signs must comply with the provisions for business zoning districts in Article VII. (Ord. 31693)

sections.title: Traffic Improvement
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-1040.116. TRAFFIC IMPROVEMENT.

Before the issuance of a final certificate of occupancy in Tract 3, a right turn deceleration lane must be constructed on Lancaster Road at the southern-most ingress/egress point. (Ord. 31693)

sections.title: Additional Provisions
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-1040.117. ADDITIONAL PROVISIONS.

(a) The Property must be properly maintained in a state of good repair and neat appearance.

(b) Development and use of the Property must comply with all federal and state laws and regulations, and with all ordinances, rules, and regulations of the city. (Ord. 31693)

sections.title: Compliance With Conditions
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-1040.118. COMPLIANCE WITH CONDITIONS.

(a) All paved areas, permanent drives, streets, and drainage structures, if any, must be constructed in accordance with standard city specifications, and completed to the satisfaction of the city.

(b) The building official shall not issue a building permit to authorize work, or a certificate of occupancy to authorize the operation of a use, until there has been full compliance with this article, the Dallas Development Code, the construction codes, and all other ordinances, rules, and regulations of the city. (Ord. 31693)
